checks.detail: Pass. Fresh Tester MCP observations were bound to the exact candidate path and Godot 4.7 main scene. The project launched into a visible native 1280×720 placeholder room with floor, walls, ceiling, collision-backed bounds, stable lighting, and asymmetric cyan/amber orientation cues. Editor and runtime logs contained no missing-resource, script, debugger-break, or boot errors. Source and scene inspection found no authored FPS map, production weapon/hands, HUD, minimap, enemy package, decorative collection, or runtime content dependency. Compared with the PRD effect-imagination image, the current-phase framing and exposure remain readable while the intentionally deferred industrial detail, weapon, HUD, and enemies are correctly absent.

Pass. White-box inspection found restart owned by the unchanged _reset_to_spawn() path and exclusively bound to physical F6 (physical_keycode 4194337), with no R event or duplicate binding; the live InputMap independently reported restart: F6 (physical). Ordinary physical WASD and mouse-look changed position and yaw/pitch inside the bounded room. On two separately displaced and rotated attempts, physical F6 restored position (0,0.9,5.4), velocity (0,0,0), yaw 0°, pitch 0°, upright camera framing, and captured mouse. A third displacement reached approximately (-1.89,0.9,1.57), yaw -21.43°, pitch -11.34°; physical R produced no change, and the matched post-probe digest retained those values. The 82° pitch clamp, active camera, floor contact, and reset implementation remain intact.

Pass. This is a narrow bootstrap verdict only: the native shell cleanly boots, exposes ordinary movement and mouse-look, remains bounded and visibly framed, and resets deterministically through F6 while R remains available for the later reload action. No later-phase map, weapon, HUD, minimap, objective, enemy, VFX, or final-presentation requirement was added to the verdict.

required_criteria.requirement: Launch a minimal native Godot prototype with a simple bounded placeholder room, a player camera and ordinary keyboard/mouse input. This is an intentionally rough first increment: do not import the authored FPS map, real weapon or hand assets, HUD package, minimap package, enemy package or decorative asset collection. Verify the game starts without a black screen, missing-resource error or direct dependency on final content.

Use ordinary input to look and move the placeholder player inside the bounded prototype. Require stable camera framing, a visible floor, predictable input capture/release and a deterministic restart state. Placeholder geometry is permitted and expected; production scale, authored landmarks, weapons, HUD and map quality are explicitly out of scope.

Issue one narrow bootstrap verdict for the launchable placeholder loop. Accept only a real runnable shell and basic camera/input evidence; do not expand this first phase into map import, weapon implementation, HUD, minimap, enemy AI or final presentation.
